web.title: Audio Tags 101: Directing emotional TTS in Eleven v3 - ElevenLabs
web.description:
- [Eleven v3](https://elevenlabs.io/v3)

Audio Tags are bracketed, natural-language cues, such as [laughs], [gasps], [excited], and [worried], that Eleven v3 reads as performance direction rather than words to speak. When you write a script for a text to speech model, inserting these Audio Tags gives you granular control over the emotional delivery of your writing.

Audio Tags strip away that guesswork, giving you full control over an emotional text to speech performance.

## Summary
- Audio Tags are bracketed cues like [shouts] or [excited] that direct emotion, pacing, delivery, and tone within TTS in Eleven v3.
- Eleven v3 doesn’t support SSML but replaces it with Audio Tags for a more natural writing experience.
- Tags range across a few categories, such as emotions, delivery and pacing, human reactions, accents, and sound effects.
- You can access Audio Tags on ElevenLabs via the UI or through the API.

## Audio Tags vs. SSML
Eleven v3 doesn’t support SSML break tags or the rest of the SSML tag set. Instead, Audio Tags, punctuation, and the very fabric of a text’s structure take over the role, all while offering granular control over delivery.

You can use the table below to map out common SSML tags to the Eleven v3 equivalent.

What it does

Stresses a particular word

Shifts pitch lower

[drawn out] or [slowly]

Emotional tags like [excited]

Emotional TTS tags like [softly] or [sorrowful]

From a writer’s perspective, adding [whispers] to a line takes much less effort than configuring a [prosody](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/what-is-prosody) rate.

## What can you do with Audio Tags?
### Precision delivery control for AI speech
You can control the pacing of speech with Eleven v3 with Audio Tags or through punctuation.

## Emotional TTS is available on the API
Audio Tags work the same way through the [Text to Speech API](https://elevenlabs.io/text-to-speech-api) as they do within the ElevenLabs UI. Write the tag inline with the script text, and the API will return the tagged performance in the generated audio, from audiobook pipelines to ad voiceovers.

## Audio Tags and emotional TTS FAQ
### Does ElevenLabs support SSML?
Eleven v3 doesn’t support SSML, but offers a better alternative in the form of Audio Tags. You can use natural language to write emotions into your scripts, or build contextual pacing through punctuation and emphasis.

web.title: Eleven v3 Audio Tags: Expressing emotional context in speech
web.description:
Emotions shape how we speak — not just what we say but how we say it. With Eleven v3 Audio Tags, you can now infuse AI speech with emotional nuance, adding tension, warmth, hesitation, or relief to any line.

Using bracketed cues like [sigh], [excited], or [tired], you can direct the emotional delivery of a voice model — moment to moment.

## From tone shifts to emotional beats
Eleven v3 captures that through layered tags.

web.title: Best practices | ElevenLabs Documentation
web.description:
## Prompting Eleven v3
### Audio tags
Eleven v3 introduces emotional control through audio tags. You can direct voices to laugh, whisper, act sarcastic, or express curiosity among many other styles. Speed is also controlled through audio tags.

Some tags work well with certain voices while others may not. Don’t expect a whispering voice to suddenly shout with a `[shout]` tag.

#### Voice-related
These tags control vocal delivery and emotional expression:

```
[whispers] I never knew it could be this way, but I'm glad we're here.
```

web.description:
# ElevenLabs v3 Audio Tags User Guide: Mastering Emotional Voice Control
![Eleven Labs AI Voice with emotion](https://jonathanmast.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/whitebeardwizard_3D_cartoon_animation_style_Disney_Pixar_qual_1ccbcade-3015-4ace-a95c-485022f42d89_3-1024x574.jpg)

This groundbreaking model transforms simple text narration into dynamic, emotionally rich performances that rival human speech delivery [2](https://elevenlabs.io/hi/blog/eleven-v3-situational-awareness) [6](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/articles/35869142561297-How-do-audio-tags-work-with-Eleven-v3-Alpha).

## What Are Audio Tags and Why They Matter
These tags give users the ability to add emotions like `[happy]`, `[excited]`, and `[nervous]`, delivery styles such as `[whispers]` and `[shouts]`, and even non-verbal reactions including `[laughs]`, `[sighs]`, and `[gulps]` [6](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/articles/35869142561297-How-do-audio-tags-work-with-Eleven-v3-Alpha) [13](https://elevenlabs.io/pl/blog/eleven-v3-situational-awareness).

## Emotional Expression Tags
ElevenLabs v3 supports a wide range of emotional tags that transform the AI’s vocal delivery [6](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/articles/35869142561297-How-do-audio-tags-work-with-Eleven-v3-Alpha) [12](https://www.aibase.com/news/www.aibase.com/news/18702) [13](https://elevenlabs.io/pl/blog/eleven-v3-situational-awareness).

These emotional tags work by providing the AI with contextual cues about the intended mood of the speech [2](https://elevenlabs.io/hi/blog/eleven-v3-situational-awareness) [5](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/articles/14187482972689-How-to-produce-emotions).

## Delivery Style Control
Professional content creators have found delivery style tags especially useful for audiobook production and video narration [4](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/eleven-v3) [10](https://the-decoder.com/elevenlabs-eleven-v3-lets-ai-voices-whisper-laugh-and-express-emotions-naturally/).

## Conclusion
The technology enables creators to direct emotional expression, delivery style, non-verbal reactions, and even environmental sound effects with remarkable precision [1](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/v3-audiotags) [6](https://help.elevenlabs.io/hc/en-us/articles/35869142561297-How-do-audio-tags-work-with-Eleven-v3-Alpha) [13](https://elevenlabs.io/pl/blog/eleven-v3-situational-awareness).

The future of AI voice generation has arrived, and it speaks with unprecedented emotional depth and authenticity [1](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/v3-audiotags) [4](https://elevenlabs.io/blog/eleven-v3).
